summary: This is a development container configuration for PHP 8.2 that sets up a Docker-based development environment with code formatting and linting tools. It configures VS Code to automatically format PHP code using PHP-CS-Fixer and PHP CodeSniffer, installs necessary PHP development extensions, and runs Composer to add the Rector tool after the container starts.

explanations.3: The 'build' section tells Docker how to construct the container image, specifying which Dockerfile to use and what build arguments to pass to it.
explanations.5: These 'args' are variables passed to the Dockerfile during the build process, setting specific versions for PHP, Composer, and code quality tools that the container will install.
explanations.14: This mounts your local project folder on your computer to the /var/www/html directory inside the container, so changes you make locally are immediately reflected inside the container.
explanations.16: This specifies which user account inside the container will run commands—'docker' is a non-root user we use for security rather than running everything as root.
explanations.20: The '[php]' key means these settings apply only when you're editing PHP files, not other file types.
explanations.24: This tells VS Code to automatically run code fixes (like formatting) whenever you save a file.
explanations.35: This points VS Code's PHP-CS-Fixer extension to the configuration file that defines what code style rules to enforce.
explanations.38: PSR12 is a well-known PHP coding standard; this tells PHP-CS-Fixer to format code according to those rules.
explanations.46: This configures the integrated terminal inside VS Code to use bash as the shell, and specifies what icon to show for it.
explanations.54: These are VS Code extensions (plugins) that will be automatically installed in the container to help with PHP development, Docker, and code quality checking.
explanations.63: This command runs automatically after the container finishes starting, using Composer (PHP's package manager) to download and install Rector, a tool that helps modernize and refactor PHP code.
